[[cobalt-application-matrix]]
== Original applications and environment counterparts

The inventory pins all twelve Cobalt 1.92 applications. Native core types are Boost types; Wasm uses the shipped WebCPP backend. Every cell below names the actual target, thread/exception setting and host. Browser page and dedicated worker observations are separate from Node.

A controlled network counterpart changes endpoints, ports and certificate setup. It retains the application protocol. Infinite original servers are stopped after observed traffic; that does not prove graceful shutdown. Browser HTTP/WSS counterparts use host transports and do not provide raw TCP listeners.

Original examples run in Release, so an original `assert` may be disabled by `NDEBUG`. A normal exit is not evidence for an assertion that did not execute. Separate finite portable counterparts check values, cancellation and completion explicitly in the same feasible profiles.

`source-requires-exceptions` means the original application contains exception syntax. It does not mean Cobalt itself requires exceptions. Native no-EH Clang builds retain the documented upstream promise warning; only that diagnostic is nonfatal in these test consumers. P3 multi means cooperative threads, not CPU parallelism.

=== Evidence boundaries

* `pass`: the original or namespace-only migrated program ran and completed.
* `fixture`: a controlled endpoint adaptation ran against real TCP/TLS peers.
* `SDK`, `platform`, `threads`, `dependency`: the exact prerequisite is absent in that profile.
* `source EH`: explicit exception syntax in the example is rejected with exceptions disabled.
* `upstream defect`: the original failure has its own evidence; a corrected counterpart stays separately identified.

Raw JSON cells retain source hashes, implementation snapshots, commands and evidence filenames. The native Python extension is an optional CPython 3.14/nanobind experiment, not a Wasm capability. The five upstream benchmark sources remain inventoried and compile-probed; current performance uses separately identified finite matched workloads.

=== Pinned upstream benchmark sources

All five benchmark sources are compiled with the measured profiles and strict diagnostics. These are compile probes, not performance results. The original sources remain unchanged; Wasm variants change namespaces/includes and make the original concurrency-hint macro include explicit.
